title: Distributed Thresholded Counting with Limited Interaction

problem.claim: In the coordinator model, k sites communicate their inputs to a central coordinator, which must determine whether their sum exceeds a threshold.

gap.claim: The communication complexity of distributed thresholded counting remains not well understood, especially for algorithms using a bounded number of communication rounds.

contributions.claim: A deterministic algorithm achieves optimal communication complexity in α(k) rounds, where α(k) is nearly constant.
A randomized algorithm balances communication, number of rounds, and error probability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The deterministic algorithm achieves optimal communication complexity in α(k) rounds.
The randomized algorithm balances communication, rounds, and error probability.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work is situated in distributed computing.
The paper studies distributed thresholded counting in the coordinator model, where k sites communicate input information to determine whether the total exceeds a threshold.
Despite longstanding study, the communication complexity remains incompletely understood, particularly under bounded-round interaction.
Previous algorithms usually require O(łogłog N) or O(k) communication rounds.
The paper reports a deterministic algorithm with optimal communication complexity in α(k) rounds and a randomized algorithm balancing communication, rounds, and error probability.

source_observation.claim: The reported deterministic algorithm reduces the number of rounds to the nearly constant inverse Ackermann function while retaining optimal communication complexity.

interpretation.claim: In coordinator-based distributed counting, communication efficiency and interaction depth can be optimized jointly in the deterministic setting.

application.claim: When designing distributed aggregation protocols, consider bounded-round algorithms that explicitly trade off communication complexity and interaction depth.
